title: How can a bent tube be straightened to find its area?
description: A spiral tube of the same width throughout is made of nine straight parts joined at bends. The lengths are added, the corner square shared at each bend is taken away once, and the tube is imagined straightened to find its area.
teaching_notes: One idea: at each bend one corner square belongs to both arms, so it is counted twice and must be taken away once. Watch for children who add the lengths and forget the bends.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 4)
video_script.why: The child finds the area of a spiral tube by treating each straight part as a rectangle of length times width and correcting for the corner squares counted twice.
video_script.substitution: Add the lengths of the straight parts, take away one for each bend, and multiply by the width of one unit.
video_script.anchor: the spiral tube of the book, one unit wide throughout, with straight parts marked in units
video_script.payoff_line: the area of the spiral tube is one hundred twelve square units
hold_back: the area of the spiral tube is 112 square units
never_show: the area of the whole tube, before the answer beat
maths_rules: tube width 1 unit; nine straight parts of lengths 20, 20, 20, 15, 15, 10, 10, 5, 5
nine parts have 8 bends; each bend square is counted twice, so subtract 8: 120 − 8 = 112
area = straightened length × width = 112 × 1 = 112 square units
check on a small bent tube with two arms of 5: 5 + 5 − 1 = 9 unit squares, one row of 5 and a column of 4 more
video_script.design: One idea: bends count one square twice, so take one away at each bend. The spiral tube stays on stage. The small bent tube with arms of five units shows the method before the working.
open_questions: The book figure is not in the extracted text; the nine lengths (20, 20, 20, 15, 15, 10, 10, 5, 5) and the width 1 are read from the figure numbers and the worklist, and each length is taken as the whole rectangle of one straight part, as the book hint does for the bent tube with two arms of five.
